thread:
incident-bot: Pager: LATENCY_SLO_BREACH for service=redwood-runtime region=us-west-2 — p99 > 2.5s for last 5m :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Alert details: p95=850ms, p99=2670ms, streaming_stalls=3.4% (↑), affected_routes=[/v1/chat,/v1/generate]
oncall-elena: Ack, I'm on it. Paging SRE.
mike-infra: Looking at infra graphs now. Not seeing host CPU/gpu mem pressure. Kernel-level queuing looks okay.
leila-ml: I can look at model and preproc paths — suspecting tokenizer/preprocessing spikes after last prompt-template rollout.
tim-sre: Any customer reports? @amy-cs ping for customer impact.
amy-cs: Receiving 2 high-priority tickets from Beta customers — streaming stalls and partial responses. They're seeing timeouts at ~30s in client.
oncall-elena: OK, triage plan: 1) Confirm whether spike is server-side (p95/p99 dive) 2) Check recent deploys or config changes 3) Live mitigation: route traffic to lower-latency variant and disable template-level preprocessing if needed
mike-infra: I dug into ingress histograms. Tail latency concentrated on requests that run prompt preprocessing step. Breakdown from traces (sampled):
```
trace_id: 0xabc123
- recv -> auth: 12ms
- prompt-preproc: 620ms (p99)
- tokenizer: 420ms (p99)
- model-infer: 180ms
- stream-write: 40ms
```
```
metrics: tokenization_ms{route="/v1/chat"} p50=12 p95=180 p99=420
metrics: prompt_prep_ms{mode="json-mode"} p99=980
```
leila-ml: That matches my gut. We rolled out a change to prompt templates and enabled JSON mode parsing/validation in the preproc service 17m ago (deploy 1781542200).
leila-ml: The JSON-mode pre-parser validates tool schemas and injects structured tool calls — it performs `jsonschema.validate()` for each tool block which is synchronous. That can blow up CPU on long prompts.
tim-sre: Can we mitigate by disabling JSON-mode at the routing/proxy level?
oncall-elena: Yes — do fast mitigation: 1) add a request header to opt-out preproc for the canary/routing policy 2) fallback route to model-variant `redwood-lite` that has shorter prompt pipeline 3) scale preproc horizontally as short term
mike-infra: Pushing route change to traffic split now: `rbacctl route set-split --route /v1/chat --split 80:20 -> redwood-lite` — applying.
deploy-bot: Route change applied: /v1/chat split -> 80% redwood (default), 20% redwood-lite at 1781543287
amy-cs: Early signs of reduced errors from one customer after redirect to fallback variant.
leila-ml: I also pushed a hotfix to preproc to short-circuit heavy JSON validation for known tool_schema sizes > 10k chars (adds heuristic skip). Patch id: preproc-heat-1781.
oncall-elena: Good. Can we measure effect? tim-sre, mike, capture p95/p99 again in the next 2-3 minutes.
mike-infra: Updated metrics window. New numbers (2m after): p95=420ms, p99=980ms, streaming_stalls=0.9%
leila-ml: Improvement but still higher than baseline (p99 baseline ~350ms). Looks like tokenizer is still a contributor.
tim-sre: Source-level traces show that tokenization time scales superlinearly with prompt length when using the new template interpolation: `O(n * m)` where m = number of tool placeholders. One example request: 12k chars + 22 tool placeholders -> tokenization 1.1s.
leila-ml: Our template engine expands placeholders before tokenization which duplicates content; not great when placeholders are big. Rolling back that template expansion is another mitigation.
oncall-elena: Decision: 1) Keep traffic split in place, 2) disable JSON-mode globally for now (controlled flag) while we revert template expansion, 3) schedule urgent postmortem.
leila-ml: Executing global disable: `kc set env preproc ENABLE_JSON_MODE=false --namespace=preproc-prod`
leila-ml: Patch applied at 1781543420, warm restart of 4 preproc pods (rolling).
mike-infra: Observability note: rolling restarts caused a short blip in 99th quantile (~200ms) but otherwise steady.
mike-infra: New metrics (5m after mitigations): p95=300ms, p99=420ms, streaming_stalls=0.2% — back to SLO range.
amy-cs: Notifying impacted customers: sent initial statement and will follow up with RCA once postmortem complete.
oncall-elena: On-call handoff: I'm going offline in 20m, handing to @tim-sre — keep monitoring and follow up on the rollback + postmortem items.
tim-sre: Ack, I'll take lead. Action items captured: 
- [P0] Rollback template expansion permanently OR make it lazy (leila)
- [P0] Replace synchronous jsonschema.validate() with async/streaming validator or size-based bypass (leila)
- [P1] Add tokenization cost telemetry per-request (mike)
- [P2] Add circuit-breaker to stop heavy preproc for single request (>10s preproc) (tim)
- [P3] Update runbook for latency incidents to include JSON-mode flag and routing fallback (elena)
- [P1] Customer comms follow-up (amy)

oncall-elena: Thanks all. Closing paging thread when metrics stable for 30m. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident resolved: LATENCY_SLO_BREACH cleared at 1781543804 — p99 < 500ms for 10m window
tim-sre: Filing incident postmortem doc and linking tests to prevent regression (prompt template canary + tox perf test).
leila-ml: I'll attach example payloads that triggered high tokenization and propose a change to template interpolation algorithm (de-duplicate expansions, streaming tokenization).
amy-cs: I'll include affected customer list and timeline for support.
oncall-elena: Handoff completed. Going offline. :phone_off:
